artifacts.summary: Confirms the chapter-quality-check.sh stderr-into-stdout defect is isolated to one call site with a one-line fix, rules on the density-vs-presence conflict (resolution iii: fix the case-h2 fixture and add missing presence-check coverage), and flags a pre-existing shellcheck baseline across touched files.

next_steps: Run /plan 353 to create an implementation plan from this report's recommendations.

memory_candidates.content: This codebase has two sanctioned idioms for separating a collaborator's stdout (captured as structured payload) from its stderr (diagnostics) rather than merging with 2>&1: (1) direct-inherit -- drop the 2>&1 entirely so stderr flows to the caller's own fd 2 untouched, correct when the caller never needs to inspect stderr content (e.g. chapter-quality-check.sh's check_placement()); (2) capture-and-relay -- capture stderr to a mktemp file via 2>"$stderr_file" and cat it to the caller's stderr if non-empty (see orchestrate-predispatch-review.sh:466-480), correct when the caller needs to inspect/log stderr content. Default to (1) unless inspection is actually needed.
shellcheck is not on PATH by default in this NixOS environment; run it via `nix-shell -p shellcheck --run "shellcheck -x <file>"` rather than assuming it is missing.

When a test suite's two advisory checks have independent, documented firing conditions (e.g. a density-ratio check and a presence check in typst-element-lint.sh), a fixture that silently satisfies both at once can mask that only one condition is actually being isolated. Before trusting a fixture's inline comment about 'what this isolates', grep the suite for independent positive-path coverage of every check the fixture's inputs could also trigger -- a check with zero positive-path fixtures anywhere in the suite is a coverage gap worth fixing alongside the bug.
